# Three levels

Model: `levels`. Each call creates a complete slide. Inter, geometry and text sizes are fixed.

[Model index](../../../templates/MODELS.md) · [Palette and content guide](../../STUDIO-MODELS.md)

```latex
\studiosetup{palette=light}
\studiotemplate[variant=default]{levels}
```

Palette switches are available only where the original composition exists in both colours.
Unsupported explicit choices fail. A global palette leaves special compositions in their native treatment.

## Variants and named fields

### default

Original palettes: blue, light.

[Current source](../../../templates/studio/privacy-levels.tex) · [Full slot guide](../guides/privacy-levels.md)

| Field | Default | Available space |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | <code>Title</code> | 13.5% wide × 15.6% high |
| `item-one/text` | <code>Supporting explanation</code> | 41.9% wide × 10.4% high |
| `item-two/text` | <code>Supporting explanation</code> | 41.9% wide × 10.4% high |
| `item-three/text` | <code>Supporting explanation</code> | 41.9% wide × 10.4% high |

Group each row as `item-one={text={...},icon={shield}}`, then `item-two` and `item-three` from top to bottom. Use `image` or `graphic` instead of `icon` for custom artwork. Empty values hide only that field.

Omitted fields retain these descriptive defaults; empty values retain their allocated space. Numbers and charts are illustrative.

## Complete one-slide example

```latex
\documentclass[aspectratio=169]{beamer}
\usetheme{bitpolito-studio}
\usepackage{bitpolitostudiotemplates}
\usepackage[backend=biber]{biblatex}
\addbibresource{bibliography.bib}
\begin{document}
\studiotemplate[
  variant={default},
  palette={light},
  title={Title},
  item-one={
    text={Supporting explanation}
  },
  item-two={
    text={Supporting explanation}
  },
  item-three={
    text={Supporting explanation}
  }
]{levels}
\end{document}
```
